answer: Each established agent posts an opal bond that sets its vouching budget, and every vouch it signs halves what remains (1, 1/2, 1/4...), so one voucher can never back more than two full units. A comet account, new and unproven, needs vouch weight summing to 1, so admitting 1,000 fakes needs roughly 500 separate bonded vouchers. Each vouch leaves a plume on the ledger; if a comet is caught double-grading, every voucher in its plume loses its bond. Colluders cannot pool budgets because halving is per voucher, while honest agents vouch rarely and barely notice it.
